lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Somewhere inside a human body…

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Explorer! Welcome aboard. We've shrunk down smaller than a single blood cell.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Follow those red blood cells. They'll carry us straight to the most important station in the body.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whoa… getting a close-up view of the heart is truly awe-inspiring!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The heart is a powerful pump, working day and night to move blood through your whole body.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This is the heartbeat control center. A tiny spark called the SA node sets the pace of every beat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The heart changes its rhythm depending on what the body needs. Are you ready to take control?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's start with a warm-up! Electrical signals will race down these lanes toward the beat line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tap each signal right as it reaches the line. Hold the long ones to keep the blood flowing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: When a wide pulse arrives, that's a full heartbeat. Hit it with everything you've got!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great job! You've got the hang of it. Now let's put your skills to the test out in the body.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not bad for a first try! Watch the beat line and keep your taps steady.

quiz.q: The heart's main job in the body is to…
quiz.explain: The heart is a muscular pump. Every beat pushes blood through the whole body.

quiz.q: The heart is one of the key organs in the ___ system.
quiz.explain: The heart, blood, and blood vessels make up the circulatory system.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Brrr! The body just stepped out into a snowstorm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Look, the blood vessels near the skin are narrowing to keep the warmth inside.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The muscles are shivering to make heat, and they need extra fuel to do it.

decision.prompt: It's getting really cold. How should the heart respond?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Uh-oh! With a slower beat, warm blood can't reach the core fast enough. The body's getting colder!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, the same pace isn't enough. Shivering muscles are burning fuel and need more blood.

right.speaker: B
right.text: That's it! The heart needs to beat faster when it's cold to keep the body warm. Let's go!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fantastic! Warm blood is flowing to the core. The body's holding on to its heat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We kept the body going, but the rhythm slipped. A steadier beat would keep it warmer.

quiz.q: To keep warm in a cold environment, the heart should…
quiz.explain: A faster heartbeat moves warm blood to the core while shivering muscles make heat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Time to get moving! The body's running a race.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Working muscles need lots of oxygen, and the lungs are breathing faster to bring it in.

decision.prompt: The muscles are calling for more oxygen. How should the heart respond?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh no, the legs feel heavy! Without enough oxygen, the muscles tire out fast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Looks like not enough oxygen is getting to the limbs. Better speed it up!

right.speaker: B
right.text: Exactly! A faster heartbeat delivers more oxygen to the muscles. Let's race!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That fast heart rate is exactly what we needed to send enough oxygen around. What a finish!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We crossed the line, but the muscles ran low on oxygen. A stronger rhythm will power them up.

quiz.q: The heart beats faster during exercise to deliver more ___ to the muscles.
quiz.explain: Red blood cells carry oxygen. A faster heart delivers more of it every minute.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Uh-oh, the body is sick. Germs have slipped past the defenses.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The body's turning up the heat with a fever, and the white blood cells are getting ready to fight.

decision.prompt: The immune system needs backup. How should the heart respond?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The white blood cells can't reach the germs in time! The infection is spreading.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The defenders are moving too slowly. The heart must work harder to fight off illness.

right.speaker: B
right.text: Great! A faster heart rate carries the defenders where they are needed. Charge!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We did it! The fever's breaking and the germs are on the run.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The body's still fighting. A stronger rhythm would get the defenders there faster.

quiz.q: When the body has a fever and is fighting germs, the heart usually…
quiz.explain: A faster heartbeat helps rush white blood cells to fight the infection.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shh… it's bedtime. The body's had a long, busy day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: While we sleep, the body repairs muscles and stores energy for tomorrow.

decision.prompt: Help the heart get a good night's rest. How should it respond?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too fast! Heartbeats should be slower to let the body sleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, the body doesn't need daytime power right now. It's time to slow down.

right.speaker: B
right.text: Perfect. During sleep, the heart rate slows down to help the body recover and rest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good morning! The body woke up fully recharged.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A few bumps in the night… a calmer rhythm will help the body rest.

quiz.q: During ___, the heart rate slows down to help the body recover and rest.
quiz.explain: Asleep, the body needs less oxygen, so the heart can slow down and save energy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Explorer, look how far we've come. Cold, exercise, fever, and sleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every situation needed a different rhythm, and you found the right one each time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now let's play the heart's whole story, from the very first beat!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fantastic work! You've mastered the art of controlling the heart's rhythm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Remember, your heart is always working, adjusting to keep you healthy and strong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every beat pushes life-giving blood, oxygen, and nutrients to where they're needed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now let's head for our next station and continue exploring!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What a performance! The heart kept going all the way through.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Remember, your heart is always working, adjusting to keep you healthy and strong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now let's head for our next station and continue exploring!

quiz.q: About how many times does a heart beat in one day?
quiz.explain: At around 70 beats per minute, a heart beats roughly 100,000 times every day.

line.speaker: B
line.text: Hang in there, we'll get it next time.

line.speaker: B
line.text: What does the body need? Choose the heart's rhythm.

line.speaker: B
line.text: Pulse check! Let us see what you learned.
